![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14098036/assets/77accc09333167b5d086558ab56120a240f31e03c9c575a22d55f4d76b6f7c45.png)

The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=1,$ the particle is located at the position $x=2.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=6?$

The position of the particle at $t=6$ is $x=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=6$ is equal to its position at $t=1$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [1,6].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(6)=x(1)+{\int }_{1}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(1)=2$, and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{1}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=1$ to $t=6.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{1}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t=\frac{3}{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(6)=2+\frac{3}{2}=\frac{7}{2}.
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=6$ is $x=\frac{7}{2}.$
